name: ARM SVE/SVE2 (Scalable Vectors, 128-2048 bit)
description: Vector-Length Agnostic (VLA) SIMD with predication. Eliminates scalar tail loops via predicated operations. SVE2 adds cryptographic and permutation instructions. Vector width determined by hardware (128-bit on V2, 256-bit on V1/Graviton3, 512-bit on A64FX).

key_instructions.purpose: Byte permutation from single source vector using index vector. SVE equivalent of NEON TBL. Core of LUT-based decode. Scales with VL.
key_instructions.note: V1: 256-bit (2x128 internally). V2: 128-bit native. TBL throughput is excellent on both.

key_instructions.intrinsic: svmad_u8_z(svbool_t pg, svuint8_t op1, svuint8_t op2, svuint8_t op3)
key_instructions.purpose: Predicated multiply-add: (op1 * op2) + op3. Computes (val_hi * 64) + val_lo in one instruction for 6-bit merge.
key_instructions.note: Predicated: only active lanes compute. Inactive lanes zero or merge.

key_instructions.purpose: Generate predicate mask for loop control. Creates mask where lanes [0..n) are active. THE key VLA instruction: enables processing arbitrary-length inputs without scalar tail loop.
key_instructions.note: Used at start of each loop iteration: pg = svwhilelt_b8(i, n);

key_instructions.purpose: Compress active elements to front of vector, removing inactive. Could help with whitespace-skipping compaction.
key_instructions.note: SVE2 only. Only works on 32/64-bit elements, not bytes. Limited applicability for byte-level base64.

key_instructions.intrinsic: svmatch_u8(svbool_t pg, svuint8_t op1, svuint8_t op2)
key_instructions.purpose: Compare each element in op1 against all elements in op2 (segment). Useful for character classification: check if each byte is in the valid Base64 alphabet.
key_instructions.note: SVE2 only. Powerful for validation but limited to 16-element segments.

key_instructions.intrinsic: svld1_u8(svbool_t pg, const uint8_t *base) / svst1_u8(svbool_t pg, uint8_t *base, svuint8_t data)
key_instructions.purpose: Predicated load/store. Only active lanes access memory. Enables safe processing of input tails without over-read/over-write.
key_instructions.note: First-faulting variant (LDFF1) suppresses faults on inactive lanes. Useful for speculative loads.

base64_applicability: NOVEL CONTRIBUTION AREA. No production SVE base64 decoder exists. SVE advantages for base64: (1) VLA: single binary runs on all SVE widths (128-2048 bit), (2) Predication eliminates scalar tail loop entirely, (3) WHILELT + predicated load/store handles arbitrary lengths cleanly, (4) TBL instruction is efficient for lookup. Challenge: the 4:3 decode ratio (every 4 input -> 3 output) complicates VLA output addressing. Proposed solution: process VL-aligned chunks and use predication for the final partial chunk. SVE2's MATCH instruction could enable efficient validation.
